This is the part most players don't know. Where a tunnel exit lands is probabilistic by zone type — for example, a Tunnel Black High exit has an 85% chance to connect to another high-tier Blackzone, 10% to a low Blackzone, and 5% to a medium. Tunnel Deep Main and Deep Secondary both route predominantly to lower tunnels (64% Tunnel Low, 23% Tunnel Medium, 13% Tunnel High). This is why deeper roads tend to stay deep — they're weighted to loop inward.

Avalonian Portals can be found in every area above Tier 4 on both the Royal Continent and the Outlands. The tier of the entry zone dictates the tier of the Road you enter. Guilds can also place Hideouts inside Roads at sites with a blue power crystal, which lets them fast-travel directly in without hunting a portal.

content.text:
Subdomains are configured with a CNAME record through your DNS provider. For more information, see Managing a custom domain for your GitHub Pages site. A www subdomain is the most commonly used type of subdomain. For example, www.example.com includes a www subdomain. www subdomains are the most stable type of custom domain because www subdomains are not affected by changes to the IP addresses of GitHub's servers. A custom subdomain is a type of subdomain that doesn't use the standard www variant. Custom subdomains are mostly used when you want two distinct sections of your site. For example, you can create a site called blog.example.com and customize that section independently from www.example.com. An apex domain is a custom domain that does not contain a subdomain, such as example.com. Apex domains are also known as base, bare, naked, root apex, or zone apex domains.

Verifying your custom domain prevents other GitHub users from using your domain with their repositories. 

If you configure the correct records for each domain type through your DNS provider, GitHub Pages will automatically create redirects between the domains. For example, if you configure www.example.com as the custom domain for your site, and you have GitHub Pages DNS records set up for the apex and www domains, then example.com will redirect to www.example.com. If you instead configure example.com as the custom domain, then www.example.com will redirect to example.com. Automatic redirects also apply to other subdomains, as www.blog.example.com will redirect to blog.example.com or vice versa. It is not possible to configure a domain that starts with www.www.. Austin, Texas · Established under 26 U.S.C. § 508(c)(1)(A)

BIOGRAPHY
For Public Distribution, Grant Applications, and Organizational Records
THE FOUNDING STORY
For eleven years, Rickey Jay Bennett II preached the Word of God on the streets of
America.
Not from a pulpit. Not with a salary or a congregation or a denominational charter behind her. She preached
from sidewalks and shelters and bus stations, in cities from one coast to the other, as a traveling minister
without credentials or institutional backing — only a Bible and a conviction that would not leave her alone.

willing to work and cannot is not facing an economic problem. They are facing a spiritual crisis. A violation of
something God intended.

labor market that can strip a willing worker of every foothold before they can find the next one. She lost jobs
as quickly as she found them. She preached the dignity of labor from the exact position of someone the
economy had left behind — not despite the contradiction, but because of it. Because she understood from
the inside what it means to be willing, to be able, to be trying, and still to be without.

problem and eleven years of preaching at it, the gap between what the mandate promised and what the
world delivered had become too wide to keep standing in. The reassurance that God would provide had
grown hollow — not because it was false, but because provision requires more than proclamation. It requires
action. It requires someone to build the thing that should have already existed.

the work mandate of 2 Thessalonians 3:10 is not a comfort. It is a command — and a command carries with
it a corresponding obligation. If those who are willing to work must work, then the community of faith must
ensure they have the capacity to do so. When technology displaces a worker from their vocation, the Church
does not get to offer thoughts and prayers. The Church is obligated to equip.

waiting for someone to fulfill it. She is building it so that the next generation of displaced workers does not
have to wait as long.
The mandate stands. Now we build.

Rickey Jay Bennett II is the Founder and Minister of The Thessalonian Mandate Institute, a Faith-Based
Organization established in Austin, Texas, under 26 U.S.C. § 508(c)(1)(A), dedicated to the workforce
retraining of individuals displaced by automation and artificial intelligence.

organizational vision. An independent minister and street preacher for over eleven years, she proclaimed the
scriptural mandate of dignified labor across the United States while navigating the very conditions of
economic displacement that the Institute exists to address. Her ministry was conducted without institutional
affiliation or denominational support — grounded entirely in scripture and sustained by sincere religious
conviction.

biblical tradition of vocation that extends from the creation mandate of Genesis 2:15 through the wisdom
tradition of Proverbs and the apostolic teaching of Paul. She understands technological displacement not as
an economic phenomenon but as a spiritual crisis — a forcible removal of human beings from the vocation
God assigned them at creation — and has constructed a comprehensive doctrinal response to that crisis in
the founding documents of the Institute.

For website, press materials, and introductions
Rickey Jay Bennett II is the Founder and Minister of The Thessalonian Mandate Institute. She preached the
dignity of labor on the streets of America for eleven years — without a pulpit, without credentials, without
institutional backing — while navigating the same economic displacement her organization now exists to
address. She founded the Institute on the conviction that the work mandate of scripture is not a comfort but a
command, and that the community of faith is obligated to equip those who are willing to work but cannot. She
is based in Austin, Texas.

world that did not always make space for her — which is precisely why she understands what it means to be

evidence that the mandate applies without exception, that dignity in labor belongs to everyone the economy
has left behind, and that the God who commands work does not first require conformity.

PART I: THE SCRIPTURAL FOUNDATION
1.1 The Primary Mandate — 2 Thessalonians 3:10
The doctrinal center of this organization is the explicit apostolic command recorded in Paul's second letter to
the church at Thessalonica:
2 Thessalonians 3:10 (NIV)
"For even when we were with you, we gave you this rule: 'The one who is unwilling to work shall not
eat.'"
This verse is not a suggestion. It is not a cultural observation. Paul frames it explicitly as a rule — a binding
apostolic directive given in person and now committed to writing for permanence. The Greek word used is
parangello (parangello), the same term used for military orders. An organization that equips people to fulfill
this obligation is not merely performing a social service — it is performing a ministry of obedience to divine
command.
1.2 The Creation Mandate — Genesis 2:15 and Genesis 3:19
Genesis 2:15 (NIV)
"The Lord God took the man and put him in the Garden of Eden to work it and take care of it."
Genesis 3:19 (NIV)
"By the sweat of your brow you will eat your food until you return to the ground."
Work precedes the Fall. In Genesis 2:15, God assigns Adam the task of tending and keeping the garden
before sin enters the world. Work is therefore not punishment — it is the original vocation of humanity,
established in the image of a God who himself worked in creation. The Fall does not eliminate the work
mandate; it makes it harder. The sweat is new. The calling is not.
1.3 Excellence in Craft as Virtue — Proverbs 22:29
Proverbs 22:29 (NIV)
"Do you see someone skilled in their work? They will serve before kings; they will not serve before
officials of low rank."
The wisdom tradition of Israel elevates skilled work as the pathway to honor, influence, and dignity. The
Hebrew word mahir — skilled, swift, sharp, ready — describes mastery that comes only through deliberate
practice. The cultivation of technical skill is a sacred pursuit. Training people in the crafts of the modern
information economy is the active cultivation of mahir in obedience to the wisdom mandate of scripture.
1.4 Labor as Worship — Colossians 3:23
Colossians 3:23 (NIV)
"Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for the Lord, not for human masters."
Every act of labor, performed with full devotion, becomes an act of worship. The secular and the sacred are
not divided categories in Pauline theology — they are unified under the lordship of Christ. A displaced worker
who learns a technical craft and builds products for human flourishing is, in the fullest theological sense,
working for the Lord.
1.5 Preparation as Wisdom — Proverbs 24:27
Proverbs 24:27 (NIV)
"Put your outdoor work in order and get your fields ready; after that, build your house."
Build capacity before building security. Develop productive ability before establishing stability. The deliberate
work of equipping people with productive capacity is not merely practical advice — it is biblical wisdom in
action.
PART II: THE HISTORICAL AND CONTEXTUAL FOUNDATION
2.1 The Church at Thessalonica
Thessalonica was the capital of the Roman province of Macedonia — a major Mediterranean seaport, a hub
of trade, commerce, and skilled labor. The church Paul founded there consisted largely of manual laborers
and working poor whose productive capacity was being disrupted by theological confusion. Some had
stopped working, convinced the imminent return of Christ made continued labor unnecessary. Paul's rebuke
uses the Greek ataktos — a military term meaning out of formation, undisciplined. The structural parallel to
technological displacement is exact, not metaphorical.

2 Thessalonians 3:7–9 (NIV)
"We were not idle when we were with you, nor did we eat anyone's food without paying for it. On the
contrary, we worked night and day, laboring and toiling so that we would not be a burden to any of
you... in order to offer ourselves as a model for you to imitate."
Paul was a tent-maker who practiced his craft even during full-time apostolic ministry. He had the right to be

2 Thessalonians — a letter written to working poor in a Mediterranean trade city whose livelihoods were being disrupted. That's not metaphor, that's the exact situation again.

An open book or scroll with a subtle tech element embedded — a cursor, a chip, a signal line. Faith and technology in one mark.

Strong serif wordmark — TMI stacked or inline — with the mandate as a tagline beneath. The name itself carries enough weight if the type is right.

Classical symbol of learning and light, modernized with clean lines. Universal, cross-cultural, immediately understood as education.
